sources.title: Microsoft Form 8-K: change in reportable segments

claims.text: Microsoft sells business and consumer software, cloud infrastructure, devices, advertising, and gaming. Customers pay for subscriptions, usage, licenses, hardware, and services. Its Nasdaq common-stock ticker is MSFT.

evidence.locator: Cover page; Item 1, General / What We Offer

claims.text: FY2026 used Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Effective FY2027, reporting changes to Agents and Infra and Devices and Consumer. Azure becomes more narrowly consumption-based infrastructure; historical segment comparisons require the September recast.

evidence.locator: Updated segment reporting / Changes to segments and investor metrics

claims.text: The September reporting presentation groups Microsoft 365 and GitHub with Azure in Agents and Infra. This combines enterprise applications and agents with the infrastructure that runs workloads; Devices and Consumer includes Windows, Xbox, and search/advertising.

evidence.locator: Updated segment reporting: Agents and Infra; Devices and Consumer

claims.text: Distribution combines direct enterprise and public-sector sales, partners serving organizations of varied sizes, OEM software preinstallation, and digital marketplaces. Enterprise consumption, employee subscriptions, PC purchasing, advertising, and gaming create distinct demand exposures.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Distribution, Sales, and Marketing; Operating Segments

claims.text: Microsoft operates cloud infrastructure and sells the applications above it. In July management described its own Maia and Cobalt chips alongside NVIDIA and AMD hardware; datacenter deployment and utilization constrain how quickly demand becomes billable capacity.

evidence.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, cloud infrastructure and silicon

claims.text: Competition differs by product: Office faces established and AI-first application vendors; Dynamics faces cloud and on-premises business software; Azure faces competing infrastructure and platform services. This packet does not establish relative market shares.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Operating Segments / Competition

claims.text: Interpretation: integrating enterprise applications, identity, developer tools, and infrastructure may reduce customer integration work and increase switching costs. Product breadth and distribution support that mechanism, but do not establish permanent pricing power or immunity from substitutes.

evidence.locator: Updated segment reporting: stack layers and Agents and Infra
Item 1, Intelligent Cloud / Competition, identity and security portfolio; Distribution, Sales, and Marketing

claims.text: Interpretation: Copilot adoption, premium Microsoft 365 products, and Azure consumption can expand spending within existing accounts. The July call attributed Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud growth to premium products and seat additions; sustained growth requires useful deployment and sufficient capacity, not merely signed contracts.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood prepared remarks, Microsoft 365 Commercial and Azure results

claims.text: For FY2026 ended June 30, GAAP revenue was USD 331,839 million, operating income USD 155,237 million, net income USD 133,749 million, and diluted EPS USD 17.95. FY2025 revenue was USD 281,724 million. Net income includes investment effects; the issuer separately reconciles non-GAAP results excluding OpenAI investment impacts.

evidence.locator: Income Statements; Fiscal Year 2026 Results; Non-GAAP Definition

claims.text: At June 30, 2026, cash, equivalents, and short-term investments were USD 76,843 million. FY2026 operating cash flow was USD 182,935 million and cash additions to property and equipment were USD 115,948 million. Cash capex excludes noncash finance-lease additions; lease obligations also matter when assessing financial capacity.

evidence.locator: Balance Sheets; Cash Flows Statements
Amy Hood prepared remarks, capital expenditures and finance leases

claims.text: The September 15 announcement identifies Satya Nadella as chairman and CEO, Amy Hood as CFO, and Sandra E. Peterson as lead independent director. Combining chair and CEO roles makes independent board oversight relevant; a full compensation and ownership review remains outstanding.

evidence.locator: Annual shareholders meeting hosts

valuation-context.unavailable: A current share price, fully reconciled enterprise value, and forward consensus were not sourced. No current multiple or fair-value estimate is asserted.

claims.text: The issuer lists October 28, 2026 for FY2027 first-quarter earnings. Interpretation: the release should test cloud demand and spending efficiency and provide the first quarterly reporting under the new segment structure. A scheduled release does not imply a favorable result.

evidence.locator: Upcoming Microsoft FY27 Q1 Earnings / next earnings release date
Item 7.01, effective FY2027 reporting structure

claims.text: Material risks include cybersecurity failures, competition, regulatory constraints, and cloud capacity or supply shortfalls. Interpretation: persistent weak utilization or cloud monetization relative to infrastructure spending would undermine the growth thesis even if reported revenue keeps rising.

evidence.locator: Item 1A, competition, cloud and AI strategy, cybersecurity and infrastructure risks

claims.text: Scenario assumptions: bull—AI applications and Azure utilization reinforce each other; base—growth continues with capital demands; bear—capacity commitments outlast profitable demand. Track cash conversion, lease obligations, and comparable segment margins. These are research hypotheses without assigned probabilities or price targets.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood prepared remarks, capex, cash flow and FY27 outlook

claims.text: Microsoft and Palantir announced a government-cloud and classified-network partnership on August 8, 2024. It combines Azure infrastructure and Azure OpenAI with Palantir platforms; the announcement made classified availability subject to authorization. This is an integration relationship, not evidence of exclusivity or identical competition.

evidence.locator: Partnership scope and authorization condition

claims.text: September 2, 2026: Microsoft announced its FY2027 segment redesign. September 15: the board declared a USD 0.98 quarterly dividend per share, payable December 10 to holders of record November 19. The declaration is not a completed payment.

evidence.locator: Dividend declaration
Item 7.01

gaps: Evidence cutoff 2026-10-18; financial statements cover FY2026 ended 2026-06-30. SEC submissions and selected issuer developments were checked; this is not an exhaustive news or legal-event review.
FY2027 segment recast is sourced, but a full historical restatement of segment financial metrics has not been entered into this packet.
Current valuation, detailed debt maturities, compensation incentives, customer concentration, and competitive market shares require further work.
The July earnings call predates September segment changes; its old segment-specific guidance must not be treated as current comparable guidance.
